classification.difficultyReason: Solve derivative trigonometric equations with the correct quadrants, use the second derivative to classify extrema, and combine inflections and endpoints into the sketch.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the first and second derivatives of $y=\cos x+\sqrt3\sin x$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the stationary points in the domain $0\le x\le2\pi$, and use the second derivative to determine their nature.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-\sin x+\sqrt3\cos x&=0\\\tan x&=\sqrt3\\x&=\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{4\pi}{3}\\y\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)&=\frac12+\sqrt3\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\&=2\\y\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)&=-\frac12+\sqrt3\left(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\&=-2\\y''\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)&=-2<0\\y''\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)&=2>0.\end{align*}$$
Thus $\left(\frac{\pi}{3},2\right)$ is a maximum and $\left(\frac{4\pi}{3},-2\right)$ is a minimum.

$$\begin{align*}-\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x&=0\\\tan x&=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\\x&=\frac{5\pi}{6},\frac{11\pi}{6}.\end{align*}$$
Here $y''=-y$, so $y=0$ at both candidates. The concavity is down on $\left(0,\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$, up on $\left(\frac{5\pi}{6},\frac{11\pi}{6}\right)$ and down on $\left(\frac{11\pi}{6},2\pi\right)$. Both candidates are points of inflection.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Hence sketch the curve, for $0\le x\le2\pi$.

answer.short: Sketch through $(0,1)$ and $(2\pi,1)$, with the maximum, minimum and inflection points from parts b–c.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=1\\y(2\pi)&=1.\end{align*}$$
The curve increases to $\left(\frac{\pi}{3},2\right)$, decreases through $\left(\frac{5\pi}{6},0\right)$ to $\left(\frac{4\pi}{3},-2\right)$, then increases through $\left(\frac{11\pi}{6},0\right)$ to $(2\pi,1)$. Apply the concavity found in part c.

spec.description: Equation-driven closed-domain sketch with corrected numerical tick order and a labelled minimum abscissa.
spec.mathematics: y=cos(x)+sqrt3 sin(x); endpoints (0,1),(2pi,1); max (pi/3,2), min (4pi/3,-2); inflections (5pi/6,0),(11pi/6,0).
